subject: Recap + action map: HelixCare reserved GPU scope & risk matrix
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@helixcare.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + action map: HelixCare reserved GPU scope & risk matrix

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the proposed scope for a reserved (dedicated) GPU pool, and the immediate next steps so your procurement and infra teams can move forward.

Quick summary of pain & goals:
- Production latency spikes at peak (inference p95 ~1.6s for 2k token median requests) are causing poor UX; caching not fully leveraged across current setup.
- Regulatory requirement to limit PHI exposure: need tenant isolation and SOC2-compliant audit trails.
- Predictable monthly spend for high-throughput batch workloads (batch jobs + streaming inference).

Proposed Redwood reserved pool (high level):
- Pool size: 8 x A100-80GB equiv (initial), with defined burst capacity to 12 GPUs for scheduled batch windows.
- Isolation model: single-tenant pool with network segmentation + encrypted KV cache; optional per-team namespaces (soft multi-tenancy) if you need cost-sharing.
- Latency SLOs: target 99th percentile token latency <= 2.0s for real-time routes; throughput SLOs to sustain 120 qps steady-state for critical endpoint.
- Operational: 24/7 on-call during rollout, tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdown via Redwood Console.

Risks / open questions we logged during the call:
1) Peak burst profile quantification — we need representative traffic traces or a 48 hr sample to validate burst sizing.
2) Data residency / KMS: do you require HSM-backed key management (on-prem KMS) for the private pool?
3) Contract cadence: do you prefer quarterly ramp vs annual reserved commit for pricing?

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- HelixCare: share 48 hr request trace + example payloads (action: Samir) — due 2026-08-11.
- Redwood (Rishi): produce a technical runbook with isolation diagram + recommended kernel/quantization profile — due 2026-08-10.
- Redwood (Irene): send draft SLA and procurement checklist + cost estimate for 8 GPU pool and a 12 GPU burst option — due 2026-08-09 (attached).
- HelixCare procurement: confirm preferred billing cadence and legal contact — due 2026-08-13.

Attachments: SLA draft (v1), isolation diagram, and the call notes workbook (stubbed filenames below).

If that aligns, I’ll kick off the runbook and loop in our solutions engineer for a short technical deep dive next week. Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi

Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + action map: HelixCare reserved GPU scope & risk matrix

Irene — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming alignment on most items. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Burst needs: the busiest windows are monthly batch jobs (end of month billing) and ad-hoc model retrains. We can provide traces, but note that burst-to-12 should be considered conservative; our infra team expects occasional peaks up to 16 for <2 hour windows.
- KMS: we prefer cloud KMS with customer-managed keys (not HSM) for now; we can revisit if audits demand HSM later.
- Latency: the 2.0s p99 target is acceptable as a business KPI, but we also need guidance on degradation policy when burst capacity is exhausted (prefer graceful fallback to smaller model variant).

Action — I’ll get the 48 hr traces and a short note from procurement on billing preference by 2026-08-11.

—Samir
Samir Khan
Head of ML Platform, HelixCare
samir.khan@helixcare.ai

Samir / Priya — quick technical follow-up after reviewing the notes and the initial usage numbers Samir mentioned on the call.

Short answers to your asks:
- Burst headroom to 16 GPUs: we can support a scheduled autoscale window for end-of-month batches with pre-warmed kernels and a warm-up policy (30–45 min). That will increase cost but avoids cold-start latency.
- Graceful degradation: our routing policy supports fallback to a quantized model variant or to a smaller context route; we can attach automatic fallbacks by route with priority weighting per endpoint.
- KV cache isolation: per-namespace encrypted KV caches are supported; we’ll document encryption-at-rest details and audit log granularity in the runbook.

Technical asks for sizing: please provide
1) 48 hr request traces (timestamps, route id, tokens/request) — needed for batching/throughput simulation.
2) Typical sequence length distribution (50/median/95) and model variants in use.

I’ve started the isolation diagram and included three options in the runbook draft (single-tenant pool, soft namespaces, fully isolated per-team). I’ll attach the diagram to the shared Drive by Monday.

If HelixCare wants to validate the model fallbacks, we can arrange a 2-hour lab session (demos + performance sweep) in the week of Aug 16.

Cheers,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

- Legal: we need a copy of the standard SOC2 addendum/sample DPA; can you include that in the next packet?

We’ll send the 48 hr trace and sequence length distribution by Tue morning (2026-08-11). Please also include cost delta for "with burst to 12" vs "with burst to 16" in Irene's updated estimate.
